{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2014–15 |team=Iowa State Cyclones |image=Iowa State Cyclones logo.svg |conference=Big 12 Conference |short_conf=Big 12 |CoachRank=19 |APRank=9 |record= 25–9 |conf_record= 12–6 |head_coach= [[Fred Hoiberg]] |hc_year= 5th |asst_coach1= Matt Abdelmassih |asst_coach2= Charlie Henry |asst_coach3= Cornell Mann |stadium=[[Hilton Coliseum]] |champion= [[2015 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 Conference tournament champions]] |bowl= [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = round of 64 }} {{2014–15 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2014–15 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team''' represented [[Iowa State University]] during the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Cyclones were coached by [[Fred Hoiberg]], who was in his fifth season. They played their home games at [[Hilton Coliseum]] in [[Ames, Iowa]] and competed in the [[Big 12 Conference]]. They finished the season 25–9, 12–6 in [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] play to finish in second place. They defeated [[2014–15 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]], [[2014–15 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]], and [[2014–15 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] to become champions of the [[2015 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 Conference tournament]] to earn an automatic bid to the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. In the NCAA Tournament they were upset by [[2014–15 UAB Blazers men's basketball team|UAB]] in the first round. At the conclusion of the season, head coach [[Fred Hoiberg]] accepted the same position with the [[Chicago Bulls]] of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]. ==Previous season== The [[2013–14 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Cyclones]] finished 28–8, and 11–7 in [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] play to finish in a tie for 3rd place in the regular season conference standings.{{cite web | url=http://www.big12sports.com//pdf1/134781.pdf?DB_OEM_ID=10410 | title=Big 12 Conference }} They defeated [[2013–14 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]], [[2013–14 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]], and [[2013–14 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]] to become champions of the [[2014 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 Conference tournament]] to earn an automatic bid to the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. In the NCAA Tournament, they defeated [[2013–14 North Carolina Central Eagles men's basketball team|North Carolina Central]] and [[2013–14 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen, where they lost to [[2013–14 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]]. ===Offseason departures=== {| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center" |+ style="{{CollegePrimaryStyle|Iowa State Cyclones|border=0|color=white}}" | Offseason departures |- align=center ! style="{{CollegeSecondaryStyle|Iowa State Cyclones|border=0}}" |Name ! style="{{CollegeSecondaryStyle|Iowa State Cyclones|border=0}}" |Position ! style="{{CollegeSecondaryStyle|Iowa State Cyclones|border=0}}" |Reason for departure |- | [[Melvin Ejim]] || Forward || Graduated |- | [[DeAndre Kane]] || Guard || Graduated |- | Tyler Ellerman || Forward || Graduated |- | Percy Gibson || Forward || Transferred to [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland]] |- | K.J.
